children: stock surged ~9% to ~$3.18 on Tuesday after the company’s top executives disclosed fresh purchases of the company’s shares, putting a spotlight on insider confidence as the stock remains sharply lower for the year.
According to the latest SEC filing, CEO Anthony Ping Yeow Tan purchased 10.35M Class A ordinary shares for approximately $29.9M, paying a weighted average of $2.8866 per share.
The purchases were made across transactions ranging from $2.83 to $2.91, the filing showed. Tan now beneficially owns 10.78M shares.
The buying was not limited to the CEO. President and Chief Operating Officer Alexander Charles Hungate also bought 299,571 shares for about $867K, at a weighted average price of $2.8936.
His transactions ranged from $2.87 to $2.91, bringing his beneficial ownership to 6.41M shares.
The insider purchases come after a difficult year for Grab. Despite Tuesday’s rally, the stock remains 38.18% lower YTD, compared with a 13.43% gain for the S&P 500 (
, with a 4.80 rating score, while Seeking Alpha analysts rate the stock Buy at 4.14, and the SA Quant system has a Hold rating with a 3.18 score.

For investors, the key development is not simply Tuesday’s 9% jump but whether the unusually large insider purchases can mark a turning point for a stock that has significantly lagged the broader market this year.
